components.input_conditions: Probability simplex with n>=2 and Euclidean squared norm objective.
components.parameter_and_cost_changes: n is dimension and s is support cardinality. They are not interchangeable with oracle budgets.
components.preserved_model_properties: Compact convex domain, convex continuously differentiable objective, exact gradient 2x and curvature 4.
remaining_obligations: A resource lower-bound application must prove its own resource-to-support implication.

construction.definition: For integer n>=2, D=Delta_n={x in R^n:x_i>=0, sum_i x_i=1}=conv{e_1,...,e_n}; f(x)=sum_i x_i^2. For integer 1<=s<=n consider outputs with card(x)<=s. The global minimizer is the uniform vector u=(1/n,...,1/n).
construction.hidden_objects: None. There is no hidden parameter, resisting oracle or information concealment.
construction.parameters: n>=2 and 1<=s<=n are integers. Objective normalization is ||x||_2^2, without a factor 1/2. Curvature is C_f=4. The singleton n=1 case is excluded here; its curvature would be zero.
construction.public_information: The entire objective, dimension and domain may be public. The output support restriction is an additional algorithm/output condition, not an oracle-imposed information restriction.

escape_conditions.epistemic_note: Exact consequence of the published fixed Theorem.
escape_conditions.statement: Allowing the dense output u=(1/n,...,1/n) attains the optimum directly from public data.

escape_conditions.epistemic_note: Complete local example and transfer check supplied below.
escape_conditions.scope: LMO models without the explicit vertex-returning realization.
escape_conditions.statement: An exact LMO need not return a vertex on ties. A dense minimizer may defeat an argument that counts one coordinate atom per call.

hardness_claims.algorithm_coverage: Every feasible support-constrained output, regardless of how it was computed. For randomized algorithms the bound holds pointwise whenever the support promise holds for each realized output. No unrestricted algorithm or Oracle Complexity lower coverage is asserted.
hardness_claims.missing_lifting: No unrestricted Oracle Complexity lifting is supplied. An arbitrary algorithm may directly output u.
hardness_claims.regime_note: For integers n>=2, 1<=s<=n, minimum support-constrained objective is 1/s and minimum primal gap is 1/s-1/n; equality is attained by s coordinates equal to 1/s. The bound becomes zero at s=n.

local_arguments.argument: The simplex is nonempty, closed and bounded in R^n and hence compact; nonnegativity and the sum constraint are preserved by convex combinations. The polynomial f has gradient 2x and Hessian 2I, so it is continuously differentiable and convex. For y=x+gamma(z-x), direct expansion gives f(y)-f(x)-<y-x,2x>=gamma^2||z-x||_2^2. Thus Eq. (3) gives C_f=2 sup_{x,z in Delta_n}||z-x||_2^2. Nonnegativity gives <x,z>>=0, and ||x||_2^2<=sum_i x_i=1, likewise for z, so ||z-x||_2^2<=2. For n>=2, x=e_1 and z=e_2 attain 2. Hence C_f=4. This calculation is local; the original page 5 also states the curvature value.
local_arguments.name: Model membership and curvature; local calculation distinct from source text

local_arguments.argument: For d in R^n and z in Delta_n, <z,d> is a convex combination of the coordinates of d and is at least min_i d_i. Therefore the stated vertex oracle is exact. If a procedure starts from a vertex and every output is a convex combination only of that vertex and T returned coordinate vertices, its support is contained in their union and has size at most min(n,T+1): coordinates outside the union vanish term by term. Applying published thm.P011.sparse_bound@1 yields the corresponding support bound, without any claim that arbitrary algorithms obey this generation rule. For exact Frank-Wolfe specifically, the first step has gamma_0=1 and discards the initial point; with vertex-returning LMO, after K>=1 updates induction on the union of returned supports gives card(x_K)<=min(n,K), even if x_0 was dense. These conditional implications are local, not original unrestricted oracle claims. If ties permit arbitrary minimizers, take x_0=u: its gradient is constant in all coordinates, so every point of Delta_n minimizes the linearization, including dense u. With gamma_0=1 the next iterate may be u. Thus exactness alone does not imply one-coordinate returns or sparse output.
local_arguments.name: Vertex realization, conditional support transfer and escape; complete local argument

oracle_realizations.choices_and_history: Deterministic smallest-index tie breaking is one explicit realization; no adaptive hiding is used. The oracle depends only on the current query.
oracle_realizations.cost: Charge one gradient query and one LMO query separately. A direct dense implementation computes the gradient and scans the LMO direction in O(n) arithmetic each. The support budget s is not an oracle query count.
oracle_realizations.information_bottleneck: There is no information bottleneck. The obstruction is the imposed support of the output; each returned atom is a single coordinate vertex.
oracle_realizations.information_to_error: Published thm.P011.sparse_bound@1 gives f(x)-f(u)>=1/s-1/n for every feasible output with card(x)<=s. Turning a call budget into s additionally requires a proved output-generation rule; a dense output need not satisfy that rule.
oracle_realizations.query_and_feedback: Gradient query at x returns 2x. An LMO query with direction d in R^n returns e_i where i is the smallest index attaining min_j d_j. It is exact since <z,d>=sum_j z_j d_j>=min_j d_j for every z in Delta_n, with equality at e_i.
oracle_realizations.sampling_and_reuse: No sampling. Repeated queries may reuse identical deterministic feedback; no statistical independence is assumed.

summary: The public simplex quadratic has exact support-constrained error 1/s-1/n. A vertex-returning LMO realizes sparse iterates, while unrestricted dense output escapes the obstruction.
title: Squared Euclidean norm on the simplex: a sparse-output obstruction
use_when: An algorithmic argument independently restricts feasible output support to at most s coordinates.
